speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are here for dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help me narrow this down, have you noticed if your vision swims or if the room seems to spin when you turn your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis.

Based on your history of a sustained, constant spinning sensation starting this morning, along with nausea and relief from diphenhydramine, these symptoms align with inner ear inflammation rather than a transient positional trigger. While your garlic intake is noted, it does not explain this specific acute vestibular presentation. I will proceed with a diagnosis based on the clinical picture of unilateral vestibular hypofunction.
